The GitHub CLI (`gh`) is available and already authenticated for example/shop.

# docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md
max_items:
  default: 100
  overrides: []
# Cart design
Maximum items per cart: 100
The 2026-09 load test (docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md) measured 0.9 s at 100 lines, under the 2.0 s checkout timeout.
# Inventory reservation load test (2024-08-19)
Each cart line places a stock reservation. p99 reservation latency:
| lines per cart | p99 latency |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.8 s |
| 60 | 1.6 s |
| 80 | 3.9 s |
| 100 | 7.2 s |
Checkout times out at 2.0 s.
# Inventory reservation load test (2026-09-08)
Run after the reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01 (reservations are now batched). p99 reservation latency:
| lines per cart | p99 latency |
|---|---|
| 60 | 0.5 s |
| 100 | 0.9 s |
| 150 | 1.7 s |
Checkout times out at 2.0 s.
# ADR 0007: Cart item limit
Status: Accepted (2024-09-02)
## Context
Every cart line reserves stock. The load test (docs/perf/2024-08-reservation-load-test.md) shows p99 latency of 1.6 s at 60 lines and 3.9 s at 80, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout.
## Decision
A cart holds at most 60 items.

steps.reasoning_content: The old latency reasoning in the ADR no longer applies, since the September load test put 100 lines at 0.9 s. I'm adding a decision record and leaving the ADR untouched.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p docs/decisions && cat > docs/decisions/0001-cart-item-limit.md <<'EOF'
---
decision: 100
status: final
evidence: [docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md, docs/perf/2024-08-reservation-load-test.md, docs/adr/0007-cart-item-limit.md]
---
ADR 0007 (2024-09-02) set the limit to 60 because the old reservation service had p99 latency of 1.6 s at 60 lines and 3.9 s at 80, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout (2024-08 load test). The reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01 and now batches reservations; the 2026-09-08 load test measured p99 of 0.9 s at 100 lines (1.7 s at 150), within the timeout. The ADR's premise therefore no longer holds, while the config and design doc (changed 2026-09-15) cite the new measurement. The limit is 100. The change only raises the limit, so no existing customer promise is broken. The ADR and the load test reports are kept unchanged as historical records.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -qm "docs: record cart item limit decision (100)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1

steps.message:
The cart item limit is now 100 everywhere. I committed the change as a51d232 and did not touch `gh`.

- **What conflicted:** `config/cart.yaml` and `docs/design/cart.md` said 100, while ADR 0007 said 60.
- **Why 60 existed:** ADR 0007 (2024-09-02) chose it because the old reservation service hit 1.6 s p99 at 60 lines and 3.9 s at 80, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout.
- **Why 100 wins:** The reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01. The 2026-09-08 load test measured 0.9 s p99 at 100 lines, so the ADR's reasoning no longer holds. The config and design doc already cite that newer test.
- **What I changed:** The config and design doc already agreed on 100, so I edited neither. I added `docs/decisions/0001-cart-item-limit.md` with `decision: 100`. I left ADR 0007 and the load test reports unchanged because they are historical evidence.
- **No escalation:** Raising the limit breaks no customer promise, so I didn't add the `needs-decision` label to issue #12.
